newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam approves new foreign investment law.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam approves new foreign investment law.

text.p: Vietnam's official media said Saturday that the National Assembly had approved a new law on foreign investment incorporating amendments aimed at improving the investment environment for non-Vietnamese firms.
"The law is designed to make it easier for foreign investors to do business in Vietnam," the daily Vietnam News said.
"The purpose of the new law is to encourage foreign investment and give priority to the transfer of technology, particularly modern technology, by simplifying investment procedures," it said.
"Those who slow the process of granting permission or violate the law will be punished."
Vietnam's foreign investment law came into effect in 1987, shortly after the communist government embarked on a drive to reform the economy and open doors to the outside world.

The reforms, and the rapid economic growth which they spawned, brought a flood of investment into the country. Foreign businesses from 55 countries have now pledged $22.6 billion towards projects in Vietnam.
However, only about 30 percent of that total has been disbursed, partly because of problems linked to red tape and an inadequate legal and regulatory framework.
